scope: Concurrent real provider investigations through validation-only transparent local data proxies

report.summary: During the requested 17-minute investigation window, checkout-service logs show Java heap exhaustion and high heap pressure in version v1.4.2. Threshold-validated aggregate p95 latency remained near 0.48s and the 5xx error rate near 0.20pp, with no detected anomalies. The log findings support heap pressure as a likely failure mechanism, but do not establish its underlying cause or the extent of user impact.

likely_causes.title: Java heap exhaustion or severe heap pressure in checkout-service
likely_causes.rationale: The OutOfMemoryError samples directly indicate Java heap exhaustion, and the GC warnings reporting 92% heap usage support significant heap pressure. These observations support this failure mechanism but do not identify what caused the pressure or prove an aggregate latency or error-rate impact.

supporting_evidence.detail: Two ERROR samples for checkout-service version v1.4.2 report `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`, with sampled timestamps from 2026-10-25T23:44:10+00:00 to 2026-10-25T23:51:10+00:00.
Two WARN samples for checkout-service version v1.4.2 report `GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%`, with sampled timestamps from 2026-10-25T23:46:10+00:00 to 2026-10-25T23:51:10+00:00.

next_steps: Inspect JVM heap, allocation, garbage-collection, and heap-dump data around the reported errors to identify the source of heap pressure.
Check instance-level restarts, OOM events, and affected-request logs to assess scope and user impact; steady aggregate metrics do not rule out localized failures.
Review version v1.4.2 changes and runtime heap configuration, without assuming a deployment regression from the version label alone.
Verify log-query behavior and coverage: the targeted OutOfMemoryError query returned zero documents, while the broader ERROR query returned two samples containing that message.
Collect request-rate and resource measurements before attributing heap pressure to traffic or resource contention; no such findings were supplied.

report.summary: During the requested 43-minute investigation window, payment-service p95 latency held steady near 0.91s and its 5xx error rate held steady near 1.72pp; neither threshold-validated metric was anomalous. Logs show repeated timeouts calling fraud-api and payment authorization errors reporting fraud checks unavailable. These logs support investigating the payment-service-to-fraud-api dependency path, but do not establish fraud-api's internal failure mechanism or prove a broader latency increase. Fraud-api log queries returned no documents, which is not evidence that the service was healthy.

likely_causes.title: Failure or slow responses in the payment-service-to-fraud-api dependency path
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated upstream timeout warnings and fraud-check-unavailable authorization errors support this dependency path as a candidate cause. They do not prove the cause originated within fraud-api or establish temporal ordering.

supporting_evidence.detail: 19 payment-service WARN documents reported “upstream timeout calling fraud-api after 2000ms” (version v1.4.2; sampled occurrences from 2026-10-25T23:18:11+00:00 to 2026-10-25T23:54:11+00:00).
6 payment-service ERROR documents reported “PaymentAuthorizationException: fraud check unavailable” (version v1.4.2; sampled occurrences from 2026-10-25T23:20:11+00:00 to 2026-10-25T23:50:11+00:00).

next_steps: Inspect fraud-api metrics, traces, and dependency telemetry for the investigation window. The supplied fraud-api ERROR and timeout queries returned zero documents; this absence does not establish health.
Use distributed traces and payment-service request outcomes to determine whether the fraud-api timeouts account for the authorization errors and identify where the delay or failure occurs.
Check request-rate measurements if traffic changes are relevant; no request-rate evidence was supplied.
Continue monitoring payment-service latency and error metrics, which were steady and not anomalous in the supplied threshold-validated findings.

report.summary: During the requested 91-minute query interval, cart-service had a threshold-validated 5xx error-rate increase from 3.71pp to 15.00pp (4.0x), while p95 latency remained steady near 0.23s. Retrieved ERROR logs repeatedly report a NullPointerException in PromotionEngine.applyDiscount at PromotionEngine.java:88 (version=v1.5.0). This exception is a supported candidate contributor to the elevated errors, but the findings do not directly link exceptions to failed requests or establish exact causal timing. No WARN documents or PromotionEngine-matching documents were returned; these empty query results do not establish service health.

likely_causes.title: NullPointerException in PromotionEngine.applyDiscount
likely_causes.rationale: Repeated errors at the same application method support a null-handling defect as a likely contributor to the elevated 5xx rate. The evidence does not prove each exception produced a 5xx response or establish whether the errors began before the rate increase.

supporting_evidence.detail: Threshold-validated 5xx error rate rose 4.0x, from 3.71pp to 15.00pp; anomaly_detected=True.

20 retrieved ERROR samples report NullPointerException at com.shop.cart.PromotionEngine.applyDiscount(PromotionEngine.java:88), version=v1.5.0; sample timestamps range from 2026-10-25T23:36:12+00:00 to 2026-10-25T23:55:12+00:00.

next_steps: Correlate traces or request-level logs for these exceptions with 5xx responses to quantify their contribution.
Inspect the inputs and null-handling logic at PromotionEngine.java:88, and compare v1.5.0 with the previous version and deployment history.
Review request-rate and error-count time series; the supplied findings do not establish whether request volume changed.
Treat the zero-result WARN and PromotionEngine queries as limited query results, not evidence that related events or service problems were absent.
